name: French Dominoes
description: French Dominoes is a cut-throat domino game from the Caribbean (particularly Jamaica) featuring a distinctive cross-shaped tile layout. Played with a double-six domino set, it requires players to form a cross pattern with tiles before extending outward, combining careful strategy with luck. The game emphasizes blocking opponents while emptying one's own hand.

content.text: French Dominoes is a cut-throat domino game from the Caribbean (particularly Jamaica) featuring a distinctive cross-shaped tile layout. Played with a double-six domino set, it requires players to form a cross pattern with tiles before extending outward, combining careful strategy with luck. The game emphasizes blocking opponents while emptying one's own hand.
French Dominoes originated in the Caribbean, particularly Jamaica, despite its European name. It likely developed from European domino traditions adapted to Caribbean gaming culture.
Dominoes, paper and pencil for scoring.
Shuffle all 28 dominoes face-down. Each player draws 7 dominoes and places them in their rack. Remaining 0 dominoes stay as the draw pile.

items.text: Alternative Zero Scoring: The double-zero domino counts as 10 points instead of 0, preventing anomalies where a player with only a blank tile in hand wins the round scoring 0.
Casual Rules (No Pass Penalty): Three consecutive passes do not incur a 10-point penalty; the game simply passes back to the first player.
Two-Player French Dominoes: Each player draws 12-13 dominoes. Play proceeds similarly but with only two competitors. Winning scores and blocking rules may be adjusted.
